turns.prompt_text: Hi, is it better to drain batteries all the way or keep them fully charged? I'm talking about reusable batteries.
turns.response_html:
Whether you should drain a battery or keep it topped off depends entirely on the chemistry of the battery. Modern electronics use different rules than the rechargeable batteries from twenty years ago.

Lithium-ion (Li-ion) & Lithium-polymer (Li-po)

Common in: Smartphones, laptops, tablets, and modern power tools.

  • The Best Strategy: Keep them between 20% and 80%.
  • The "Deep Discharge" Myth: You should not drain these to 0%. Doing so puts significant stress on the battery and can even cause it to fail permanently if the voltage drops too low.
  • Heat is the Enemy: Keeping a battery at 100% while it is plugged in and generating heat (like gaming on a laptop) can degrade it faster. Most modern devices have "Optimized Charging" features that stay at 80% until you actually need the full charge.

Nickel-Metal Hydride (NiMH)

Common in: Rechargeable AA and AAA batteries (e.g., Eneloop, AmazonBasics).

  • The Best Strategy: You don't need to drain these to zero every time, but a full discharge once every few months helps.
  • Memory Effect: They suffer slightly from "lazy battery effect" if they are only partially discharged and then recharged repeatedly.
  • Storage: If you aren't using them, store them with a partial charge (around 40%) in a cool, dry place.

Nickel-Cadmium (NiCd)

Common in: Very old cordless drills or vintage electronics.

  • The Best Strategy: Drain them completely.
  • The Memory Effect: These are famous for the "memory effect." If you only use 30% of the battery and then charge it, the battery eventually "remembers" that 30% mark as its new zero point, drastically shortening its life.

Summary Table

Battery TypePreferred StateAvoid This
Lithium-ion20% to 80%Draining to 0%
NiMH (AA/AAA)Mostly chargedConstant trickle charging
NiCd (Old)Fully cycled (100% to 0%)Frequent "top-off" charging

Pro Tip: If you are putting a device away for several months, never store it at 0% or 100%. Aim for 50% to keep the chemistry stable while it sits idle.
